text: dsh-protect-generated-files 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的开发工具插件，在工具执行前检查文件写入、编辑和 shell 原地修改。它识别锁文件、常见构建或代码生成路径，以及文件头中的生成标记；命中时会阻止修改并告诉模型应修改哪个源文件、使用什么生成命令，也可配置为请求用户审批。用户可通过设置面板调整识别规则、排除路径、shell 检查和重试行为，适合希望避免智能体直接改坏生成产物的开发者。通过 DSH 插件命令安装，不需要额外密钥或外部服务。

dsh-protect-generated-files checks DSH file edits and shell commands for lockfiles, generated paths, and header markers. It blocks matching changes and tells agents how to regenerate them. Users can configure path rules, shell checks, and approval behavior. No API key is required.
别让 DSH 智能体直接改 package-lock 或 pnpm-lock 这类锁文件。
我想阻止模型手动编辑带有 DO NOT EDIT 标记的代码。
让 DSH 检查 sed -i 或 tee 对生成文件的修改。
编辑构建产物时，能不能提示我去改源代码并重新生成？
Can DSH stop agents from editing generated files and point them to the source to change?
I need a guard against shell commands that overwrite generated code or lockfiles.
dsh-protect-generated-files 的功能「识别生成文件」：在文件写入或编辑前，根据锁文件名称、内置 glob 和文件头标记判断目标是否为生成文件；命中时拒绝修改并给出对应的再生提示。
dsh-protect-generated-files 的功能「检查 shell 原地编辑」：检查配置的 bash 或 PowerShell 命令中的 sed、perl、重定向和 tee 目标；命中生成文件时，在执行前拦截。
dsh-protect-generated-files 的功能「可配置的拦截与重试」：用户可选择直接拒绝或请求审批，配置额外匹配路径及忽略规则；还可决定是否允许模型原样重试一次，以及检查多少行文件头。
能不能让修改生成目录时先弹审批，而不是直接放行？
Help agents avoid hand-editing generated code and lockfiles.

dsh-protect-generated-files README · dsh-protect-generated-files：English | [中文](README_zh.md)

Agents edit files that nobody should edit by hand. They'll patch a version number straight into `pnpm-lock.yaml`, fix a typo in `user.pb.go`, or "correct" a type in Prisma's generated client. The edit looks fine until the next `pnpm install` or `protoc` run wipes it out, or, worse, leaves the lockfile disagreeing with `package.json` in a way that takes an afternoon to untangle.

dsh-protect-generated-files README · dsh-protect-generated-files：This [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin refuses `write` and `edit` calls on generated files and lockfiles. It also refuses in-place shell edits of them (`sed -i`, `perl -pi`, `> file`, `tee file`). Instead of a bare "no", the model is told how the file is supposed to change:

dsh-protect-generated-files README · dsh-protect-generated-files：```
dsh-protect-generated-files blocked this edit to db/query.sql.go: its header says it is
generated (`// Code generated by sqlc. DO NOT EDIT.`). A hand edit will be overwritten
the next time it is regenerated, or leave it out of sync with its source.
Instead: edit the SQL queries/schema and run `sqlc generate`.

dsh-protect-generated-files README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-protect-generated-files
```

That's the `web` profile, the browser UI you start with `dsh web`. If you run DSH another way, use `headless` (scripts and CI) or `acp` (editor integrations) instead. Each profile keeps its own plugin list, so add it to every profile you use. It's active right after installing. Remove it with `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-protect-generated-files`.

dsh-protect-generated-files README · From a clone：To try local changes, build a tarball and install that:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/acus9345/dsh-protect-generated-files
cd dsh-protect-generated-files
npm install

dsh-protect-generated-files README · How it decides a file is generated：**Lockfiles, by name.** `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lock(b)`, `deno.lock`, `Cargo.lock`, `go.sum`, `poetry.lock`, `uv.lock`, `pdm.lock`, `Pipfile.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`, `composer.lock`, `mix.lock`, `pubspec.lock`, `Podfile.lock`, `flake.lock`, `gradle.lockfile`, `packages.lock.json`, `conan.lock`. Each one comes with the right command for its own package manager, for example "change dependencies with `cargo add / cargo update -p <crate>`".
section: How it decides a file is generated

text: dsh-protect-generated-files README · How it decides a file is generated：**Known output paths.** Protobuf output (`*.pb.go`, `*_pb2.py`, ...), Dart `build_runner` output, `.Designer.cs`, minified files and source maps, and anything inside `node_modules/`, `__generated__/`, `.venv/` or `site-packages/`. Build-output folders (`dist/`, `target/`, `.next/`, `vendor/` and so on) only count when they sit next to a project manifest like `package.json`, `Cargo.toml` or `go.mod`, so a source folder that happens to be called `target` isn't caught.
section: How it decides a file is generated

text: dsh-protect-generated-files README · How it decides a file is generated：**A header that says so.** It reads the first 15 lines of the file and looks for `Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT`, `@generated`, `DO NOT EDIT`, `auto-generated`, `This file was generated`, `<auto-generated>`, or a `Generated by <tool>` comment. A header that says the file may be edited ("edit freely", "safe to edit"), or a qualified `DO NOT EDIT without ...`, doesn't count. When the header names a tool it knows, the hint names that tool too: protoc/buf, Prisma, GraphQL Codegen, OpenAPI generators, sqlc, `go generate`, Drizzle, Alembic, and others. "Generated by hand" and "generated by ChatGPT" don't count.
section: How it decides a file is generated

text:
dsh-protect-generated-files README · How it decides a file is generated：The header check only applies to files that already exist. The name and path rules also cover new files, because a lockfile written by hand from scratch is just as wrong.

On Windows, where DSH runs commands through PowerShell, it also watches `Set-Content`, `Add-Content`, `Out-File` and `Tee-Object`.
section: How it decides a file is generated

text: dsh-protect-generated-files README · When a hand edit is right：It happens: resolving a lockfile merge conflict, or a one-line hotfix in vendored code while you wait for upstream. The model is told it can repeat the identical call once to confirm, and that goes through. Use `mode: ask` if you want to approve these yourself. If a directory is generated-looking but actually hand-maintained, add it to `ignore`.
section: When a hand edit is right

dsh-protect-generated-files README · Settings：The easy way: open **Plugins** in DSH's sidebar, click **dsh-protect-generated-files**, change what you want and press **Save**. It applies to the next tool call, no restart needed.

Or add a row like this to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, or to `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` for every profile. Keys you leave out keep their defaults.

dsh-protect-generated-files README · Settings：```yaml
- id: protect-generated-files
  config:
    mode: deny                    # or `ask` for an approval prompt
    extraGlobs:                   # your own generated paths, each with the hint the model gets

`extraGlobs` is the one most worth setting. Telling the model which script regenerates your code saves it from guessing.

dsh-protect-generated-files README · Development：```sh
npm install
npm test           # detector unit tests
npm run test:e2e   # real dsh runs against a scripted local model, no API key needed
```

The install test runs `dsh plugin add`, which needs `pnpm` on your PATH.
